3. Abstract Dynamic Programs
This section is a brief review of the dynamic programming framework from Sargent
and Stachurski (2025). We repeat the key definitions to make the paper partly self-
contained.
3.1. Definition and Properties. An abstract dynamic program (ADP) is a pair
(V, T), where
(i) V = (V, ⪯) is a poset and
(ii) T = {Tσ : σ ∈Σ} is a nonempty family of order preserving self-maps on V .
We call V the value space. Each operator Tσ in T is called a policy operator. Σ
is an arbitrary index set and elements of Σ are called policies. In applications, we
impose conditions under which each Tσ has a unique fixed point. In these settings,
the significance of each policy operator Tσ is that its fixed point, denoted below by
vσ, represents the lifetime value of following policy σ.
Let (V, T) be an ADP with policy set Σ. Given v ∈V , a policy σ ∈Σ is called
